name: Glycerol
what_it_is: A thick, sweet, syrupy liquid made from fats and oils, which may be from plants or animals.
why_its_added: Holds moisture so food stays soft. In slush drinks it also stops the liquid freezing solid.

india.note: Permitted at GMP level - used as needed, no fixed numeric cap in the categories found.

eu.note: Safety of acute exposure to the food additive glycerol (E 422) from beverages

vegetarian_status.means: Can be made from either plant or animal sources. The label is not required to say which one was used.

safe_daily_limit.no_number_means: EFSA has not set a number for this one. That can mean it is considered safe enough not to need a limit, or that the evidence was not sufficient to set one. The opinion itself says which.

acute_limit.unit: mg per kg of body weight, per single drink
means: This is not a daily average. It is a limit for ONE serving.
EFSA found that a single slush ice drink of 250 ml (children) or 500 ml (others)
would exceed this limit for every age group.
Reported effects in young children after high intake include nausea, vomiting,
headache, low blood sugar and loss of consciousness.
As of this check there is still no legally binding maximum for glycerol in EU
slush drinks. The UK advises that children under 7 should not drink them.

people_reports.rule: Reports are shown as reports. We count them. We never turn them into a health claim, and we never let them change the sourced facts above.

india_limits.food_category: Coffee, coffee /coffee substitutes, tea, herbal infusions, and other hot cereal and grain beverages, excluding cocoa
